sources_considered.why: Documents Anthropic's 4x price rise for Claude 3.5 Haiku over Claude 3 Haiku.
Describes Anthropic's June 2026 metering of programmatic subscription use, its stated reason, and unchanged API rates.
Aggregator; search summaries indicate ChatGPT Plus remained $20 in the US, but I did not read or cite it.
Single outlier claim of a Plus price rise to $24, contradicted by other sources; not reliable.

receipt.public_excerpt: Pricing for Claude 3.5 Haiku starts at $1 per million input tokens (~750,000 words) and $5 per million output tokens. That’s versus 25 cents per million input tokens and $1.25 per million output tokens for Claude 3 Haiku — a 4x hike.

evidence_items.explanation: An Anthropic price rise did happen. But Anthropic tied it to the new model's greater intelligence, not to costs, so it only partly matches a cost-forced price increase.

receipt.public_excerpt: Anthropic's stated reason: third-party agent tools were driving programmatic burn that "throw off our flat-rate pricing model."

evidence_items.explanation: From June 2026, programmatic use on Claude subscriptions was metered at API rates, a cost-driven repricing for one group of users. This partly fits the forecast.

receipt.public_excerpt: API token rates have not moved (and have been moving down separately, per the prior post ). The June 15 split restructures subscription plans only.

evidence_items.explanation: Shows the June 2026 change was narrow: API prices were unchanged or falling. That cuts against reading it as the broad, forced price rise the forecast implies.

unresolved_gaps: No primary Anthropic or OpenAI price-history document was read; the June 2026 change relies on a secondary write-up.
Whether ChatGPT consumer prices rose in 2026 rests on conflicting aggregator reports; most say Plus stayed at $20.
No evidence of financial collapse of either firm was found, but neither firm's profitability was checked against filings.
